title: Cardiovascular events, death and care home entry in the five years after community-acquired pneumonia: a registry-based cohort study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the long-term excess of cardiovascular events after community-acquired pneumonia. Design: registry-based cohort of 11,800 adults discharged alive in 2016 to 2021, linked to death and admission data, with matched population controls and controls admitted with other infections. Primary outcome: first cardiovascular event in the first year and in years two to five. Results and conclusions will be written after linkage and analysis.
introduction: Pneumonia is followed by an early rise in cardiovascular events, but the size of any later excess depends on confounding by frailty and on the comparison group.
methods: Registry patients and comparison groups were linked to the death register and regional admissions. Frailty came from admissions in the two years before the index date. Cause-specific Cox models were split at one year and adjusted for nine covariates fixed in advance.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present linkage completeness, absolute risks and hazard ratios by window and comparison group, and care home entry.
discussion: The discussion will compare early and late estimates with the retrieved cohorts and state which survivors need long-term follow-up.
limitations: Residual confounding; coding of causes of death; outcomes outside the region missed.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not repeat the untraced ten-year doubling figure.
summary: STROBE and RECORD structured draft with results left empty.
